in_arabic.name: حطب
in_arabic.meaning: حطب يعني الشخص الذي يجمع الحطب أو الحطاب
in_arabic.long_meaning: حطب هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي و يعني الحطاب أو الشخص الذي يجمع الحطب. و الحطب هو مصدر للطاقة و الغذاء في الماضي. و يعتبر الحطاب من المهن الأساسية في المجتمع الريفي و القروي. و اسم حطب يوحي بالصبر و العمل الجاد و الاجتهاد في الحصول على الرزق.

in_urdu.name: حطب
in_urdu.meaning: حطب کا مطلب ہے جلنے کے لئے لکڑیاں جمع کرنے والا
in_urdu.long_meaning: حطب ایک عربی نام ہے جس کا مطلب ہے حطاب یا لکڑیاں جمع کرنے والا۔ یہ نام ان مہینوں کے دوران استعمال کیا جاتا ہے جب لوگ لکڑیاں جمع کرتے ہیں تاکہ ان کی گھروں میں جلنے کے لئے استعمال کیا جا سکے۔ یہ نام صبر، محنت، اور خود کفالت کی علامت ہے۔

in_hindi.name: हातब
in_hindi.meaning: हातब का अर्थ है जलने के लिए लकड़ियाँ इकट्ठा करने वाला
in_hindi.long_meaning: हातब एक अरबी नाम है जिसका अर्थ है हातब या लकड़ियाँ इकट्ठा करने वाला। यह नाम उन महीनों के दौरान उपयोग किया जाता है जब लोग लकड़ियाँ इकट्ठा करते हैं ताकि उनके घरों में जलने के लिए उपयोग किया जा सके। यह नाम धैर्य, परिश्रम, और आत्म-निर्भरता का प्रतीक है।

in_pashto.name: حطب
in_pashto.meaning: حطب د لکړیو راټولو معنی ورکوي
in_pashto.long_meaning: حطب د یو عرب نوم دی چی د حطاب یا لکړیو راټولو مانا لری. دا نوم د هغه وخت کی کارول کیږي کله کی خلک لکړۍ راټولی تا چی په خپلو کورونو کی یی د سوځولو لپاره استعمال کړی. دا نوم د صبر، کوښښ، او خپلواکۍ نښه ده.

in_english.name: Hattab
in_english.meaning: Hattab means a woodcutter or a gatherer of firewood
in_english.long_meaning: Hattab is an Arabic name that originates from the root 'hattab' which means to gather firewood. It refers to a person who collects firewood for a living. The name Hattab has been used in Islamic tradition to signify a person who is diligent, hardworking, and self-sufficient. It also connotes a sense of humility and simplicity.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Hattab" has significant cultural importance in Islamic history as it was the title of a renowned companion of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) during the early days of Islam. Hattab ibn Abi Balta'a (R.A) was a prominent warrior and leader in the early Muslim army during the blessed period of Ridwan, which refers to the paradise of this world granted to the early Muslims as a reward for their dedication and self-sacrifice. This name has been passed down as a term of respect and admiration for those embodying the qualities of strength, courage, and steadfastness as displayed by Hattab ibn Abi Balta'a himself.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Hattab" holds spiritual significance as it is derived from the word 'hatta' which signifies a horse. In Islamic tradition, the horse is a symbol of power, strength, and sagacity, representing the human spirit striving towards the divine. The name evokes the notion of submission and dedication to Allah, symbolized in the powerful ride of a horse, carrying her rider forward towards the path of righteousness. Thus, the name "Hattab" embodies the spirit of a steadfast believer on the noble path of righteousness, keeping their focus on the Divine destination.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Hisham's 'Sirah Ibn Hisham' mentions Hattab ibn Al-Aws as one of the early supporters of the Prophet Muhammad, who pledged allegiance to him at Al-'Aqabah in 623 AD.
Al-Baladhuri's 'Ansab Al-Ashraf' describes Hattab ibn Al-Aws as a companion of the Prophet Muhammad who participated in the Battle of Badr in 624 AD.
historical_references.context: Companion of Prophet Muhammad who fought in the Battle of Badr
